text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed sharply lower for the second day in a row led by speculators and funds. Traders said the well overbought market was long overdue for a downward correction. However, with the Brazilian frost period in the background, it would be courageous to predict that the rally has come to an end. Moreover, the period of tight supplies is still ahead, so that the fall should come to a halt sooner or later. July lost $355 to close at $2,115, while September closed $370 lower at $2,130 per tonne.

Arabica futures in New York tumbled for the second consecutive session as speculators continued to frantically unload long positions. But with Brazil's two most dangerous cold-weather months coming up and world coffee stocks not expected to build until the next Central American harvest this autumn, it may be too soon to predict that the market has topped. News on Friday that Colombia was offering North American roasters about 300,000 60-kg bags of green coffee for June shipment and predictions that there would be no frost in Brazil helped to undermine sentiment. July lost 22.45 cents/lb to close at 253.95 cents/lb while September lost 13.75 cents/lb to close at 224.55 cents.

BRAZIL - Brazil's coffee region should warm up slightly in the coming days after a period of cold weather but temperatures could fall sharply next week with the approach of a new air mass, local meteorologists Somar said. The new air mass is expected to have a center of high pressuof 1,018 millibars over the center of Mato Grosso do Sul and Parana on June 8, said Somar forecaster Marcio Custodio. While this is not therefore a very strong air mass, it is worth monitoring closely because it is coming in overland and will be arriving when the country's coffee regions are already cool from the effects of last week's air mass, he added. The coldest temperatures from the approaching air mass are likely to be seen in the early morning of June 9 as the key regions of Sao Paulo and Minas Gerais are expected to be protected by cloud cover on June 8, Custodio said.

PORTUGAL - Portugal imported 53,900 bags of coffee in January 1997, 7 percent less than was imported the same month the previous year. Total imports in calendar 1996 rose by 16 percent to 727,000 bags. The main supplier of green coffee in January 1997 was Brazil with 9,500 bags against 8,700 bags the same month last year.

AUSTRIA - Austria imported 419,600 bags of coffee in January/June 1996, 16 percent less than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar 1995 dropped by 14 percent to 1.232 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/June 1996 were Costa Rica (28,500 vs 6,600 bags), El Salvador (23,000 vs 60,600 bags), Guatemala (31,900 vs 44,100 bags), Honduras (27,000 vs 42,400 bags), Brazil (50,100 vs 52,500 bags), Colombia (28,200 vs 25,800 bags) and Peru (22,500 vs 2,400 bags). The country exported 87,300 bags of coffee in January/June 1996, 18 percent less than in the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar 1995 dropped by 40 percent to 228,700 bags.
